description: FLUID publishes processing and verification code for a drone-observed dense-conflict trajectory study at urban signalized intersections. Its README links field descriptions, a processing sequence, a demonstration and the separately hosted Figshare dataset DOI. Users supply the associated raw observations and run the numbered scripts to clean trajectories and compute safety-surrogate measures; outputs are processed conflict trajectories and verification results for model testing. The documented study concerns urban intersections, not a general road network. GitHub metadata states Apache-2.0 licensing for this code. The associated Figshare data are a separate resource with their own terms, which this draft does not adopt. A limitation is that the code was not run and the source observations were not inspected; transfer to other intersection designs requires checking the field definitions and camera geometry. The pipeline can prepare trajectory cases for microsimulation or automated-driving safety evaluation. No dataset, video or model archive was downloaded. Geographic coverage in the published study is an urban intersection setting; no worldwide validity is claimed. The processed tracks can serve road-traffic simulation and model evaluation. The related model-sumo catalogue record is a possible traffic engine, but no import path was tested.
name: FLUID intersection trajectory processing pipeline
